title: Old Ideas, Novel Problems: The Instability of LLM-Based Novelty Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2610.02022v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: AI-based ideation systems are often evaluated on the novelty of their ideas, and that judgment is increasingly delegated to large language models. Such judges are typically built ad hoc and validated, if at all, on human-authored papers rather than on the generated ideas they are meant to score. So, how do novelty judges perform? Not well. We present a systematic controlled study of novelty evaluation design choices. We build an evaluation set automatically, mining OpenReview for passages where reviewers explicitly affirm or dispute a paper's originality and keeping only submissions with unanimous agreement at the extremes of their research area; we pair these with ideas from a vanilla LLM generator. Across six judges, we find that seemingly small prompt design choices have large consequences; e.g., simply telling the judge that reviewers found one idea novel and the other not can change its verdict on more than half of the identical

translated_title: 旧想法，新问题：基于大语言模型的新颖性评估的不稳定性
translated_abstract: 基于AI的构思系统（ideation systems）常常以其想法的新颖性作为评估标准，而这种判断正越来越多地交由大语言模型来完成。这类评估器通常是临时搭建的，即使经过验证，也往往是在人类撰写的论文上进行验证，而不是在其本应评分的生成式想法上进行验证。那么，新颖性评估器的实际表现如何？答案并不理想。我们对新颖性评估的设计选择开展了一项系统性的对照研究。我们自动构建了一个评估集：从OpenReview中挖掘审稿人明确肯定或质疑论文原创性的评述段落，仅保留审稿人意见完全一致、且处于其研究领域极端情况下的投稿；并将这些样本与来自标准LLM生成器产生的想法进行配对。在六个评估器上的实验中，我们发现看似微小的提示词设计选择会产生巨大的影响；例如，仅仅告诉评估器“审稿人认为一个想法新颖而另一个不新颖”，就能改变其对超过一半的相同……
tldr: 本文通过从OpenReview自动挖掘审稿人明确肯定或质疑论文原创性的段落构建评估集，系统性地对照研究了大语言模型新颖性评估器的设计选择，发现微小的提示词改动即可使评估结果在超过一半的相同想法上发生翻转，揭示了此类评估器的严重不稳定性。
en_tdlr: Through a systematic controlled study using an evaluation set automatically built from OpenReview passages where reviewers explicitly affirmed or disputed a paper's originality, this paper shows that LLM-based novelty judges are highly unstable, as seemingly small prompt design choices can flip verdicts on more than half of identical ideas.
